stepNotes.1: Scope: doctor.ts is the yargs CommandModule orchestrator (line 233); 6 pure check helpers exported for testing, 4 heavier checks delegated to doctor-storage/doctor-health/doctor-preload sidecars.
stepNotes.2: Threat model: pgrep argv is a fixed literal (no injection); port probe hard-codes 127.0.0.1; credentials check emits only provider IDs and env-var names, never values. Risk is silent error swallowing, not exfiltration.
stepNotes.3: Correctness: getServerExposureCheck and getIsolationPolicyCheck precedence logic is sound; getAxEngineDoctorCheck branches are mutually exclusive. Found require("net") at line 451 throws ReferenceError in native ESM and is masked by the catch at 476 -> F-1 MEDIUM.
stepNotes.4: Performance: handler is fully sequential despite independent probes (3 ancestor walks, 1500ms fetch, 1000ms socket, 4 NativeAddon loads, 5s pgrep, 5-file log scan). Low-frequency command so non-blocking, but Promise.all over independent checks is the single biggest perf lever.
stepNotes.5: Design: orchestration/sidecar split is healthy; sidecars accept injectable seams (inspect/run/readFile/readdir/stat/resolveSync). getServerExposureCheck hardcodes status:'ok' even when overriding a user-requested non-loopback bind -> UX nit, not a defect.
stepNotes.6: Hygiene: no unused imports or dead exports found. Inline check-numbering comments have drifted (two '11b' at lines 434+480, two '12' at 484+487, missing '11a') -> F-2 LOW, cosmetic only.
stepNotes.7: Tests: MODULE-AUDIT test list is broad CLI coverage, not doctor-specific. Pure helpers and injectable sidecars are unit-testable; the handler (line 236) is the only un-injectable surface and is acceptably uncovered.
